claims.proposition_evaluated: On August 26, 2026, Infrastructure Committee rejected administration's recommended hold on the remaining programme routes, rather than adopting it, and City Council had not adopted that hold by September 25, 2026.
claims.interpretation_notes: Infrastructure Committee neither adopted R nor carried a motion incompatible with it. Its only substantive motion to continue the previously approved scope was defeated 2–2; no member moved R. Under the brief's definitions, the committee left R without a decision. I read Version 2 of Attachment 5 as proposing evaluation and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction, but not expressly saying that all 14 listed routes must wait for that step. The proposition therefore also overstates the treatment proposed. The part established is non-adoption at committee; the parts that fail are a committee rejection and, under the primary deferral definition, rejection of a hold. Under the alternative 'did not support' reading, non-adoption at committee is Supported. For full City Council, no decision on R is shown in the records examined, so its own rejection or adoption is Not established. No later incompatible Council decision is shown; the minutes do not show an override. The previously approved CM-20-0330 scope remained the recorded Council direction. Report IS03688 separately said that construction not yet started was best postponed to 2027 because of weather; that administrative assessment was not a Council decision.

supporting_evidence.finding: Infrastructure Committee item 7.6 records no motion to adopt Recommendation 1. Salvador's motion to continue the previously approved scope, advance procurement for tender-ready routes and prepare 2027 construction was defeated 2–2. Rutherford's amendment to remove the instruction to maximize the remaining 2026 construction season was also defeated 2–2. Salvador and Janz voted for the main motion; Rutherford and Clarke voted against. Rutherford and Clarke voted for the amendment; Salvador and Janz voted against. Knack and Paquette, both committee members, cast neither substantive vote.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The committee's substantive motions, movers, named votes and results, and the absence of a vote on R in item 7.6.

supporting_evidence.finding: At item 7.6, Clarke's motion to meet privately carried 5–0; Rutherford's motion to return to public carried 5–0; Rutherford's motion to keep Attachment 4 private carried 4–0. None adopted or rejected R. The committee members were Rutherford, Salvador, Clarke, Janz, Knack and Paquette. Elliott, Morgan, Parmar, Principe, Stevenson, Tang and Wright were present as other councillors, not committee voters.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Committee minutes, August 26, 2026, roll call and item 7.6
supporting_evidence.establishes: The remaining motions at item 7.6, committee membership and attendance.

supporting_evidence.establishes: What R requested and why a committee vote alone could not approve the modified approach for Council.

supporting_evidence.establishes: The Council item was a pending notice concerning future funding options, not adoption of IS03688.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In IS03688, administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of exactly 14 named programme routes, all unbuilt as of August 10, 2026, until further evaluation, a report or a decision.
claims.interpretation_notes: The August 26 agenda and minutes list the original Attachment 5, Replacement Version 1 and Replacement Version 2, but do not specify which replacement was operative during item 7.6. I therefore used Version 2 as the brief directs. Each version lists 13 continuing entries and 14 entries listed apart. Treating combined street segments within one bullet as one entry gives 14; splitting those combined entries would increase the count. Version 2 expressly provides evaluation of the remaining routes and a Q1 2027 report for Council direction and approval, while the main report says construction not yet started is best postponed to 2027. Neither passage expressly ties construction or advancement of all 14 named routes to waiting for that evaluation, report or decision. That deferral element fails; the recommendation, count and August 10 unbuilt status hold. Under the stricter alternative requiring an explicit removal or non-proceeding statement, Version 2 is also Partially supported. Version 1 is Partially supported under both readings because its removal rule depends on route impacts and does not explicitly remove all 14 listed entries. The original is Supported under both readings: it says the 14 listed projects would be removed from programme scope for 2026 and 2027, subject to later reconsideration. The result is version-sensitive. The report says approval would require no change to the existing CM-20-0330 capital profile or associated borrowing bylaws.

supporting_evidence.finding: Recommendation 1 asks the committee to recommend Council approval of the approach in Attachment 5. The report states that Council approval is required for modified direction and that approval would not change the existing capital profile or associated borrowing bylaws.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Services report IS03688, pages 1 and 6
supporting_evidence.establishes: The recommendation, intended decision-maker and stated budget effect.

supporting_evidence.finding: Version 2 names 13 projects that 'will continue as planned' and 14 projects that 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches.' Its recommended approach calls for evaluating remaining routes and bringing a Q1 2027 report to Council for direction and approval.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The two route lists, their counts and Version 2's stated treatment.

None is recorded as under construction or complete.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Replacement Attachment 3, Locations & Status Updates, IS03688, pages 1–3
supporting_evidence.establishes: The August 10 construction status of all 14 listed-apart entries.

challenging_evidence.finding: Version 2 says the remaining routes will be evaluated and a report will seek Council direction in Q1 2027, but does not state in terms that construction or advancement of every listed-apart route waits for that step.
challenging_evidence.establishes: Why the primary express-deferral element is not established for the declared primary version.

challenging_evidence.finding: The original Attachment 5 expressly says the 14 listed projects would be removed from programme scope for 2026 and 2027, with possible later reconsideration. challenging_evidence.source_title: Original Attachment 5 and Replacement Attachment 5 Version 1, IS03688
challenging_evidence.establishes: The material difference between the original treatment and the replacement versions.

The portal blocked direct retrieval; the report and attachments were read from the supplied archived City text.
unknowns: Whether any listed route began construction between August 10 and August 26.
Whether administration intended Version 2's Q1 2027 report to prohibit all work on the 14 routes before Council direction; the text does not expressly say so.

what_would_change_my_verdict: A record showing Version 2 was operative and expressly making the 14 listed routes wait for evaluation, the Q1 report or Council decision would make the claim Supported.

claims.proposition_evaluated: From the programme's 2022 approval through September 25, 2026, Principe and Rice jointly brought two City Council motions that would each leave about CAD $50 million in CM-20-0330, direct the released funds to named destinations, and were defeated.
claims.interpretation_notes: Principe moved and Rice seconded both defeated amendments, on separate budget occasions; the stricter co-sponsorship reading therefore changes nothing. The November 2023 motion would have left CAD $50,000,000 and expressly reduced tax-supported debt funding. The December 2024 motion would have left CAD $32,700,000, outside the brief's CAD $45 million–$55 million band, and says the decrease is 'with funding from tax-supported debt' without separately directing released funds. Thus the second motion fails the primary amount and destination elements. Both motions cut at least half under the alternative amount rule, but the second still lacks an express destination under the fixed destination rule, so that alternative remains Partially supported. The originally proposed November 2023 wording directed CAD $50 million to the tax levy, but Council voted on a restated debt-reduction version; I use the version put to a vote. Rice's separate CAD $26,808,000 amendment in November 2023 was withdrawn and did not identify CM-20-0330 in its minuted text. The September 2025 suspension motion was moved by Cartmell and seconded by Principe, and was defeated, but it did not seek a budget reduction.

supporting_evidence.finding: At City Council's November 2023 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice. As put, it proposed reducing CM-20-0330 by CAD $50,000,000 with a funding reduction from tax-supported debt. Hamilton, Cartmell, Rice and Principe voted for it; Knack, Paquette, Sohi, Salvador, Tang, Rutherford, Stevenson and Wright voted against. It was defeated 4–8; Janz did not cast a vote.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council Budget minutes, November 21–28, 2023, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The first motion's final text, co-sponsors, destination, named vote and defeat.

supporting_evidence.finding: At City Council's December 2024 budget meeting, Capital Budget Amendment 2 was moved by Principe and seconded by Rice. It proposed decreasing CM-20-0330 by CAD $33,650,000 in 2025 and CAD $33,650,000 in 2026, totaling CAD $67,300,000. Cartmell, Rice, Rutherford and Principe voted for it; Knack, Sohi, Salvador, Janz, Tang, Stevenson and Wright voted against. It was defeated 4–7; Hamilton did not cast a vote and Paquette was absent.
supporting_evidence.source_title: City Council Budget minutes, December 2–3, 2024, items 5.1.1–5.1.2
supporting_evidence.establishes: The second motion's text, co-sponsors, named vote and defeat.

supporting_evidence.source_title: Capital profile CM-20-0330 and Significant Capital Project Update, September 30, 2024
supporting_evidence.establishes: The contemporaneous approved capital-budget base before the December 2024 amendment.

Its text identifies tax-supported debt as the funding source but names no destination for released funds.

challenging_evidence.establishes: Why the second defeated amendment fails two parts of the normalized proposition.

calculations_needed: November 2023: approved CM-20-0330 capital budget CAD $100,000,000; proposed reduction CAD $50,000,000; reviewer calculation CAD $100,000,000 − CAD $50,000,000 = CAD $50,000,000 remaining. It meets the primary CAD $45 million–$55 million band and the alternative at-least-half cut.

December 2024: approved CM-20-0330 capital budget CAD $100,000,000; proposed reduction CAD $33,650,000 + CAD $33,650,000 = CAD $67,300,000; reviewer calculation CAD $100,000,000 − CAD $67,300,000 = CAD $32,700,000 remaining. It misses the primary band but meets the alternative at-least-half cut.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A second defeated, jointly brought motion shown by the minutes and contemporaneous capital profile to leave CAD $45 million–$55 million, with a named destination, would make the claim Supported.
